questions.question: How should a driver test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve: let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: Which agency conducts background checks for HazMat endorsements?
questions.explanation: When applying for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts a federal security threat assessment.

questions.question: What should NOT affect your gear-shifting decision?

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's operating rpm range and your vehicle's speed. Shift up when your engine reaches the top of its rpm range or when your speedometer shows the right speed for the next gear. Do not shift based on other vehicles.

questions.question: Compared to regular trailers, tank trailers usually have:
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have higher centers of gravity, which makes them less stable. Be extra careful when turning corners or taking curves in a tank vehicle.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: When making a quick stop while carrying liquids, use the:
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles carrying liquids can roll over or skid easily. If you must stop quickly to avoid an accident, use the controlled braking method.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the start and end of your trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the start and end of your trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during your trip, not just at the beginning and end. Watch your instrument panel and gauges. Check your mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch early signs of trouble.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see what is behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children run toward them without looking for traffic.
They leave water and ice trails on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children run toward them without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks create hazards because they attract children. Children often do not look for other vehicles when running toward or away from ice cream trucks.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Okay if the weather is clear.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will turn on.
The service air line will turn on.
The emergency brakes will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will turn on.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes will turn on automatically.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block other drivers, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you drive slowly and slow down traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you. Local laws must allow the use of flashers.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require higher driving skill to operate safely than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look at the path and check for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely only on them. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle may be:

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person attending a parked placarded vehicle must be either awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. If outside the vehicle, the person must be able to see it clearly. The person cannot be inside the sleeper berth.

questions.question: What do baffled tanks do?

options.text: They are damaged and should not be used.
They control liquid surge while allowing liquids to flow through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They control liquid surge while allowing liquids to flow through.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have holes in the bulkheads that allow liquid to flow through. This reduces front-to-back surge but does not prevent side-to-side surge.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine and approaching a railroad crossing, what must you do?

options.text: Reduce your speed before crossing the tracks.
Proceed across if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: If transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track, even if there is no train.

questions.question: While driving, gauges should be:
questions.explanation: While driving, watch your vehicle's gauges for signs of trouble. Check gauges before each trip to make sure they work properly.

questions.question: Why should cargo tanks never be completely full?

options.text: Liquid needs room to expand when it gets warm.
Regulations require three feet of clearance between the liquid and the tank roof.
The tank would be too heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Liquid needs room to expand when it gets warm.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand as they get warmer. You must leave extra space in the tank for this expansion. Different liquids expand at different rates, so know the outage requirements for your specific load.
